_doc: Course 'launch_linear': one row per piece. Godot metres, Y up, course runs along +X. ramps are triangular prisms the player surfs on ('ridge' = peak up, surf both faces; 'valley' = V, surf inside). pos is the piece centre; yaw/pitch in degrees (pitch < 0 slopes downhill along +X). material names a row in materials.json. 'tuned' is set after a real playtest, every row must reach tuned=true before release. Player-facing yaws (spawn, checkpoints) are Godot degrees: -90 faces +X along the course. kind 'decor' is scenery with no collision. The ground itself is the 'terrain' block (Backdrop.gd).

world_offset_rust._doc: where the real Launch Site prefab root sits relative to the course origin, Godot metres. The prefab's main ground level is its y 3 (vents, warehouses and outbuildings stand at 2.9-3.3) and its west end is 6 m lower (floodlights and mounds at -3, range_terrain_slope climbs -3..2.9 over prefab x -153..-117); y -3 puts the main level at course y 0. The launch pad pit reaches prefab y -33 (course -36).

terrain._doc: Ground built by Backdrop.gd in course coordinates: the site levels, the launch pad pit (found at load time from the placed meshes, so it follows the player's Rust version) and hills outside site_rect. layers name materials.json rows: open ground, dirt (slopes, patches, pit floor), site concrete (patches inside site_rect). blend_materials: Rust material names on placed meshes (mounds, slopes, tower footings, pit banks) that are drawn with the terrain shader so they merge into the ground instead of standing out as smooth blobs (Rust blends them with its terrain; how exactly is unverified).

steps._doc: west of x0 the ground is 6 m lower, rising to base_y at x1: matches the two range_terrain_slope meshes (course x 27..63, y -6..-0.1)

hills._doc: height/ramp/floor/period/seed: rolling hills that start at the site_rect edge; far_*: ridged hills that rise between far_start and far_end metres out so the horizon is a skyline. A look, not Rust's terrain (unverified)

shading._doc: terrain shader uniforms. site_shade darkens the site concrete patches (pale patches read as snow); tint_a/tint_b: olive and khaki colour patches over the open ground every ~tint_period metres (a look, unverified against Rust's biome colours); scrub_*: dry scrub blobs on the open ground (one per scrub_cell metres with probability scrub_density, patchy by noise, colour is an albedo multiplier); stone_*: small pale loose stones the same way. A look standing in for ground scatter we have no meshes for (unverified against Rust's arid biome)

props._doc: Course scenery: extra copies of meshes prep already extracts for the real Launch Site (rust/mesh), set where the fixed views look so the land round the course reads as an industrial site. Our arrangement, not Rust's layout (the real placements are scene_launch_site). pos is course [x, z]; the prop stands on the ground level at x plus dy (dy copies the real placements' offsets: warehouses 0.3, awnings 0.2, floodlights and vents -0.1); awnings share their warehouse's origin, turned 180 deg as in the real placements.

roads._doc: Roads painted into the terrain shader: segments are course [x0, z0, x1, z1] (max 8), width in metres, surfaced with the materials.json row named in material and crumbling into a darker shoulder. Our layout, linking the props; not Rust's road network (unverified).
